problem_statement: The heap allocator's statistics do not record the peak (high-water mark) of heap usage. When a program allocates a large block, frees it, and then queries the heap statistics, the reported footprint returns to its previous value and there is no field reporting the largest footprint ever reached, so the maximum amount of memory the heap ever held cannot be observed. The statistics should report a maximum-footprint value that increases to at least the size of the largest allocation ever performed and is retained even after that allocation is freed; for example, after allocating roughly half of the available arena and freeing it, the reported maximum footprint should exceed half of the arena and should be larger than the maximum footprint measured before the allocation, while the other statistics (allocated, overhead, available, footprint, chunks) return to their previous values.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: The heap allocator reports statistics about its memory usage through heapmem_stats(), but the statistics structure does not include the peak (maximum) heap footprint reached over the program's lifetime, so callers cannot observe how high the heap ever grew. The maximum-allocation and statistics-validation tests rely on this peak-footprint value being present in the reported statistics and being larger after a large allocation. The required behaviour is that the reported heap statistics expose the maximum heap footprint, that it is greater after a large allocation than before, and that it reflects the size of the largest allocation made.
check_issues: `problem_statement` gives the fix away: "statistics structure does not include the peak (maximum) heap footprint reached over the program's lifetime"; "this peak-footprint value being present in the reported statistics"; "reported heap statistics expose the maximum heap footprint"; "it reflects the size of the largest allocation made". Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally

causal_chain: The max_alloc case allocates half of the available heap, frees it, and then asserts that the statistics after the allocation show a larger maximum footprint than before, that the maximum footprint is at least the allocated size, and that all other statistics are unchanged; the stats_check case asserts that the maximum-footprint statistic exceeds half of the arena size. At the base the statistics structure has no maximum-footprint field and the allocator does not record a high-water mark, so the peak never grows: these assertions cannot hold (and the test does not build at the base because the statistic is absent). With the production change the allocator records the peak footprint as the heap grows and reports it in the statistics, so the maximum-footprint value grows to at least the allocated size and is retained after the free, making both assertions pass.
